settingsHint: Business policies, document numbers and reason codes.

groupHint.stock: How stock, counts and supplier bills are controlled.
groupHint.reminders: Chasing customers who owe you money.
groupHint.printing: Lines on receipts and invoices, and how phone numbers are read.
groupHint.regional: Where your business is: the date on every sale, stock movement, receipt and journal entry is the date here.
groupHint.alerts: When Intelligence alerts you and how daily briefs are timed.
groupHint.privacy: How fast you answer people about their data, who must approve erasures, and how long records are kept.

set.negative_stock_allowed: Allow selling stock that is not there
set.payroll_unpaid_day_divisor: Days used to value unpaid leave
set.privacy_response_days: Days to answer a privacy request
set.retention_employee_records_years: Keep former employees' pay records for (years)

setHint.negative_stock_allowed: The sale still posts and an exception is raised for review.
setHint.count_variance_threshold: Stock count differences worth more than this need approval before posting.
setHint.late_posting: What happens when a document is dated in a closed accounting period.
setHint.bill_match_tolerance_percent: A bill whose cost per unit is further than this from what was ordered or received needs approval.
setHint.reminder_channel: Chase customers with overdue invoices automatically every day, or turn it off and chase by hand.
setHint.reminder_min_days_overdue: An invoice is chased once it is this many days past its due date.
setHint.reminder_repeat_days: A customer is not chased about the same invoice more often than this.
setHint.weekend_days: Leave and absence are counted without these days.
setHint.payroll_unpaid_day_divisor: A day of unpaid leave takes off basic pay divided by this number.
setHint.overtime_multiplier: Overtime is paid at this multiple of the normal hourly rate.
setHint.overtime_hours_per_month: Basic pay divided by this is the hourly rate for overtime.
setHint.phone_country_code: The calling code of your phone numbers, such as 44. National numbers are read with it.
setHint.receipt_footer: Printed at the bottom of till and payment receipts.
setHint.invoice_footer: Printed at the bottom of invoices, for example bank details or payment terms.
setHint.timezone: A name such as Europe/London or Africa/Nairobi. Business dates (what day a sale, receipt or entry belongs to) and daily briefs follow this zone.
setHint.intel_alert_channel: Message the right people when Intelligence finds something serious, or keep findings in the app only.
setHint.intel_alert_min_severity: Findings at or above this severity are sent as alerts; the rest wait for the daily brief.
setHint.intel_action_level: 1 reports only. 2 also lets managers ask a person to explain a finding.
setHint.privacy_response_days: A request is due this many days after it arrives. Use the time your law or policy asks for.
setHint.privacy_erasure_needs_approval: When on, someone other than the person who asked must approve before data is erased.
setHint.retention_notifications_days: After this, the address and text of finished messages are hidden. 0 keeps them.
setHint.retention_audit_years: For your records only: the audit trail is never deleted. Shown in the retention view.
setHint.retention_employee_records_years: Pay and employment records of a former employee are kept this long before they can be erased. 0 means no minimum.
setHint.retention_inactive_customers_years: A customer who is inactive and untouched this long is sent to the exceptions inbox for review. 0 turns it off.

numberingHint: Every document gets the next number in its series. You can change the prefix and length; the next number can only move forward.
noSeriesHint: A series is created the first time a document of that type is made.
paddingHint: Numbers are padded with zeros to this length.
reasonsHint: Reasons people must give for voids, refunds, discounts, price changes, stock adjustments and similar actions.
codeHint: Capital letters, digits and _ only, for example DAMAGED.
label: Label
requiresNote: Require a written note when this reason is used
approvalsHint: Requests waiting for you to approve or reject. You cannot approve your own request.
noPending: Nothing is waiting for your approval.
noPendingHint: New requests appear here as soon as someone submits one that needs your role.
commentHint: Optional. The person who asked will see it.
approvalRulesHint: Who must approve what, by document type and amount.
rulesNote: When a document matches a rule, it waits for someone with the approver role. Rules in several steps are approved in order.
noRulesHint: Without rules, documents are not held for approval.
docTypeHint: The document the rule applies to, as the system names it, for example stock_adjustment.
maxAmountHint: Leave empty for no upper limit.
forbidCreatorLabel: The person who created the document may not approve it
exceptionsHint: Things the system noticed that a person should look at: odd sales, stock differences, failed messages.
noOpenExceptionsHint: New items appear here when something unusual happens.
noteRequiredHint: Say what you found or did. Required.
notificationsHint: Messages sent by email and SMS, who asked not to be contacted, and which channels are ready.
subject: Subject
noMessagesHint: Messages the system sends, such as receipts and reminders, are listed here with what became of them.
optOutsHint: People on this list are never sent messages by the system, on the channel you choose.
noOptOuts: Nobody has asked not to be contacted.
noOptOutsHint: Add a phone number or email when someone asks you to stop.
recipientHint: A phone number or an email address.
removeOptOutAsk: {{who}} may be sent messages again. Continue?
channelOffHint: Messages on this channel are not sent until it is set up.
apiKeysHint: Keys let another system talk to this business. Give each key only the access it needs.
noKeysHint: Create a key when you connect another system.
keyNameHint: What the key is for, for example Website stock sync.
scopesHint: Choose what this key may do. You can only give access you have yourself.
expiresHint: Optional. The key stops working at the end of this day.
revokeAsk: Revoke the key {{name}}? Systems using it will stop working at once. This cannot be undone.
secretWarning: Copy this key now. For your security it is shown only once and cannot be viewed again. If you lose it, revoke it and make a new one.
secretUse: Send it in the X-API-Key header of each request.
myAccountHint: Your profile, password, devices and preferences.
changePasswordHint: You will be signed out on every device and must sign in again.
passwordChanged: Password changed. Please sign in again.
devicesHint: Sign out any device you do not recognise.
noOtherDevices: You are signed in on this device only.
signOutOthersAsk: Sign out of every other device? They will need to sign in again.
resetMfaAsk: Switch off two-step verification for {{name}}? Use this when they lost their phone. They will be signed out everywhere, and will sign in with just their password. If your business requires two-step verification, they must set it up again at their next sign-in.
securityHint: A code from the person's phone, as well as their password, each time they sign in.

mfaPolicy.privileged: People with powerful roles (admins, finance, payroll)

mfaPolicyHelp.off: Anyone can still switch it on for themselves from My account.
mfaPolicyHelp.privileged: Anyone who can manage users, roles, settings, approvals, accounts, payroll or imports.
mfaPolicyHelp.everyone: Every person who signs in to this business.

mfaPolicyWarn: People this applies to must set up two-step verification at their next sign-in. Until they have, they cannot do anything else. Make sure they each have an authenticator app on their phone.
mfaPolicyConfirm: Require two-step verification for "{{who}}"? Those people will be stopped at their next sign-in until they set it up.

dsr.hint: People can ask to see, correct or erase what you hold about them. Record each request, find their data, and answer within the time you have set.
dsr.verifyFirst: First check who is asking. The system cannot do this for you: write how you did it in the notes.

typeHint.access: The person wants a copy of what you hold about them.
typeHint.correction: The person says something you hold is wrong. You fix it in the customer, supplier or staff screen.
typeHint.erasure: The person wants their data removed. Some records must be kept; you will see which and why.

dsr.subject: Who it is about
dsr.subjectHint: What the person gave: an email, a phone number, an id number or a name.
dsr.notesHint: How you checked who they are, and what they asked. Do not add more personal data than needed.
dsr.noneHint: When a customer, supplier or employee asks what you hold about them, record it here.

step.searchHint: Find everything held about this person.
step.exportHint: A copy of the data, as a file.
step.eraseHint: Remove their identity from your records. Cannot be undone.
step.closeHint: Say what was done and finish the request.

search.intro: Every part of the system that keeps personal data looks for this person. An email, phone number or id matches exactly. A name can match more than one person, so those are only possible matches.
search.nothing: Nothing was found for this person. If you are sure, close the request and say nothing is held.
search.possibleWarning: Check each possible match. Tick the ones that are the same person; only ticked ones are exported or erased.

export.intro: Download everything held about this person as one file to send to them by a channel you trust. It never includes passwords or account numbers.
export.introErasure: You can give the person a copy before erasing. After erasure the data no longer exists to export.
export.logged: Every export is recorded in the audit trail: who took it, when, and how many records. The data itself is not kept.
export.gone: This erasure is finished, so the data it covered can no longer be exported.

erase.irreversibleHelp: Names, contacts and other identifying details are replaced for good. Documents and amounts stay so your books still balance.
erase.willChangeHint: Only the records found in step 1 are touched: exact matches and the possible matches you ticked.
erase.nothingSelected: No records are selected. Run the search first.
erase.mayBeKept: What may have to be kept, and why
erase.keptHint: After the erasure you will see, record by record, what changed and what was kept.
erase.noRules: These areas have no special keeping rules.
erase.approvalOn: A second person must approve before anything is erased. After you confirm, the request waits for them under Approvals. The person who asked cannot approve it. An approval rule for privacy erasure must exist, or the request is refused.
erase.approvalOff: Approval is switched off for this company, so the erasure runs as soon as you confirm.
erase.approvalUnknown: If your company requires a second person's approval (a setting), the request waits for them under Approvals and nothing changes until they approve. Otherwise it runs as soon as you confirm.
erase.typeSubjectHint: Type it exactly as the person gave it. This guards against erasing the wrong request.
erase.reasonHint: Why this is being erased, in a few words.
erase.confirmMessage: {{count}} records will be anonymised. This cannot be undone.
erase.sentForApproval: Sent for approval. Nothing has changed yet.
erase.waiting: This erasure is waiting for a second person to approve it. Nothing has been changed yet.
erase.waitingHelp: They can approve or reject it under Approvals. If they reject it, the request comes back to you.
erase.notRun: This request was closed without erasing anything.

intro.access: After you have sent the person their data, close the request and note how you sent it.
intro.correction: After you have corrected the data in the right screen, close the request and note what changed.
intro.erasure: Close the request when you have told the person what was done and what was kept.

close.noteHint: For example: sent the export by email on the due date.
close.noteRefusedHint: Why the request is refused. This is the wording you give the person.
close.confirmMessage: It will be marked finished. You cannot reopen it; record a new request if needed.
close.blockedByApproval: An erasure is waiting for approval. You can close the request after the decision.

dsr.retentionHint: What the system keeps about people, for how long, and what happens at the end. Periods come from the company settings.
dsr.noRetention: No personal data is held by the enabled parts of the system.
dsr.neverDeletedHint: These records are permanent by design. They hold ids and amounts, not identities.

support.title: Support access
support.hint: Let Ziira support look at your business to help you, for a limited time. Nothing is open unless you open it.
support.intro1: Ziira staff cannot see your data unless you give access here. Each access has a reason, a level and an end time, and you can end it at any moment.
support.intro2: Everything staff do while they are in is written to your own audit log and to the list below, with their name.
support.intro3: Read-only access can only look. Full access can also make changes, but never to passwords, two-step verification, roles, API keys or support access.
support.reasonHint: For example: help with a stock count that does not add up. Staff see this.
support.levelReadHint: They can see screens and reports. They cannot change anything.
support.levelFullHint: They can also fix records for you. Use this only when support asks and you agree.
support.noteHint: Anything else support should know, such as a ticket number.
support.revokeAsk: End this support access now? Anyone from support who is in your business is signed out straight away.
support.none: You have not given support access yet
support.noneHint: When Ziira support needs to look at your business, give access here. It ends by itself.
support.activeNow: {{name}} from Ziira support is in your business now ({{level}}), until {{until}}.
support.logNone: Staff have not done anything in your business
support.logNoneHint: When someone from support is in, each action appears here.
